title: The Libation Formula
short: Stone offering tables from sanctuaries repeat a set of words, such as a-sa-sa-ra-me (also ja-sa-sa-ra-me), i-pi-na-ma and si-ru-te; their meanings are unknown.
trouble: Students treat a-sa-sa-ra-me as a known goddess's name. Many have guessed; the word is recognized because it recurs, not because it is understood.

blocks.html: Not all of Linear A is bookkeeping. On stone offering tables from Cretan sanctuaries, carved texts repeat the same words in the same order. Scholars call this the libation formula. It is one of the most studied puzzles in the script, and a lesson in what can and cannot be said. You will need the conventional readings of Signs Shared with Linear B.

Stone offering tables from sanctuaries repeat a set of words, such as a-sa-sa-ra-me (also ja-sa-sa-ra-me), i-pi-na-ma and si-ru-te. They are recognized because they recur in the same order; their meanings are unknown.

blocks.html: Why is a recurring formula useful even unread? Repetition shows structure: which words go together, which change form, which stay fixed. That is the same kind of evidence Alice Kober used for Linear B (Alice Kober's Triplets). It can tell us that a-sa-sa-ra-me and ja-sa-sa-ra-me are forms of one word, without telling us what that word means.

Treating a-sa-sa-ra-me as a known goddess's name. Many people have guessed at it; the word is recognized because it recurs, not because it is understood. Check: in any description of the formula, look for evidence (a bilingual, a match in a known language that also explains other words); without it, a meaning is a guess.

blocks.title: Same word?
blocks.q: a-sa-sa-ra-me and ja-sa-sa-ra-me appear in the same place in the formula. What is the safest conclusion?
steps: They share most of their signs and the same position.
They are probably forms of one word, perhaps grammatical variants.
blocks.a: Probably two forms of one word, meaning unknown.
